title: Osiris myth as preserving antediluvian knowledge via Byblos

tellings.quote: So what we have essentially here is an ark floating on the water with a body of knowledge inside of it from the anti-dolivian world.

plain: The researcher Tim Alberino reads the ancient Egyptian myth of the god Osiris, whose story reaches the Phoenician port of Byblos, as a coded record of knowledge saved from a world that existed before the great flood. In his words, the myth shows "an ark floating on the water with a body of knowledge inside of it from the anti-dolivian world," meaning the world before the flood. He offers this as his own interpretation, and if right it would mean the myth preserves memory of a lost earlier civilisation.
